title: Raw restricted evaluation preserves the canonical higher-image class
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and let $q\in\mathbb N$. Use the common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention]. For $v:V\to S$ etale, put $X_V=X\times_SV$ and $j_V:X_V\to X$ [def-pc-base-change], and set $P(V)=H^q(X_{V,\mathrm{et}},j_V^{-1}F)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Let $A(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}})}((f^{-1}\mathbf Z[V])[0],F[0][q])$, with $\mathbf Z[V]$ the sheafified free abelian representable [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Let $c_V:A(V)\to P(V)$ be exactly the evaluation morphism of [def-sbc-raw-restricted-cohomology-comparison-map], using the canonical identification of its derived-section target with this cohomology group. These $c_V$ form an isomorphism of abelian presheaves, where restriction on $A$ is precomposition by the free represented map and restriction on $P$ is etale cohomology pullback with the inverse-image composition identification [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Let $\iota_V:P(V)\to(R^qf_*F)(V)$ be the canonical map sending the class of a section cocycle in an injective resolution of $F$ to its class in the cohomology sheaf of the direct-image complex [lem-weil-pbc-site-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf]. Specify the raw class map $\kappa_V$ by the following construction: take the derived adjunct $\widetilde z:\mathbf Z[V][0]\to Rf_*(F[0][q])$ of $z$, using the exact-inverse-image single-complex comparison and [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction]; apply $\mathcal H^0$, identify its source with $\mathbf Z[V]$ and its target with $R^qf_*F$ by the canonical derived-direct-image and homology shift comparisons [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and evaluate at the sheafified identity generator $e_V\in\mathbf Z[V](V)$. Equivalently this is the explicit class construction in [lem-sbc-abelian-higher-direct-image-class-compatibility]. Write $E:A^\#\to R^qf_*F$ for the unique sheafification lift of this presheaf class map [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; thus $\kappa=\eta_A\mathbin{\gg}E$. This specifies the constructed comparison intended in [lem-sbc-abelian-higher-direct-image-natural-comparison], rather than selecting an arbitrary existential witness. Then $E$ is an isomorphism and, for every $V$ and $z\in A(V)$,
$$\iota_V(c_V(z))=\kappa_V(z).$$
These assertions use the specified maps and are natural in coefficient morphisms $F\to F'$. No affine, quasi-compact, separated, proper or torsion hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03Q8, label lemma-higher-direct-images, canonical associated-cohomology-presheaf construction. Agent expansion comparing its cocycle map with the explicitly constructed raw derived-adjunction evaluation.

proof.text: Choose a bounded-below injective resolution $F[0]\simeq QI$. For each etale $V\to S$, the projection $j_V:X_V\to X$ is etale by clause (1) of the etale base-change finite-limits lemma. Its exact inverse image carries $I$ to a resolution of $j_V^{-1}F$ and preserves injectives. Both $I$ and $j_V^{-1}I$ are therefore K-injective by the bounded-below injective criterion. Consequently use the same $I$ to compute $P(V)=H^q(\Gamma(X_V,j_V^{-1}I))$ for every $V$, and $R^qf_*F=\mathcal H^q(f_*I)$. These are genuine abelian injectives; no assertion about forgotten module injectives is used. Moreover clause (1) of the etale inverse-image restriction lemma gives $\rho_{I^r}:j_V^{-1}I^r\cong I^r|_{X_V}$, natural in $I^r$, so $\Gamma(X_V,j_V^{-1}I)\cong I(X_V)=(f_*I)(V)$ as complexes; this is how a section cocycle $s\in\Gamma(X_V,j_V^{-1}I^q)$ is regarded below as an element of $I^q(X_V)=(f_*I^q)(V)$. Lean implementation: construct the augmentation generically for an additive functor, and apply preservation of homology to its quasi-isomorphism. For K-injectivity, use injective_upperStar_obj_of_etale_addCommGrp termwise and CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_injective with lower bound zero.

Put $B_V=f^{-1}\mathbf Z[V]$. Since $I[q]$ is still a bounded-below complex of injectives, the K-injective Hom comparison represents every $z:B_V[0]\to F[0][q]$ by a chain map $a:B_V[0]\to I[q]$, uniquely up to homotopy after the fixed resolution comparison. Its only nonzero component is $a^0:B_V\to I^q$, with $d_I^q a^0=0$. Write $g_V$ for the pulled-back identity section of the definition of $c$, and put $s_V=(j_V^{-1}a^0)(g_V)\in\Gamma(X_V,j_V^{-1}I^q)$. This is a cycle because $d_I^q a^0=0$.

Apply the chain-representative equality of lem-sbc-raw-restricted-resolution-evaluation to the bounded-below complex $I[q]$ and the chain map $a$ of step 2. Its restriction is K-injective by step 1 applied to this shifted complex. Under its prescribed resolutionSectionsIso, evaluation of the derived map at the degree-zero generator equals chainEvaluation of lem-sbc-raw-restricted-homotopy-sections-iso, which by that statement is the image of the generator's single-complex class under $H^0(\Gamma(X_V,a|_{X_V}))$, namely $[s_V]\in H^0(\Gamma(X_V,j_V^{-1}(I[q])))$. Undoing the shift and single-complex comparisons in the definition of $c_V$ therefore gives $c_V(z)=[s_V]\in H^q(\Gamma(X_V,j_V^{-1}I))$. Explicitly $(I[q])^0=I^q$, the shifted differential is $(-1)^q d_I$, and both the cycle subgroup and boundary subgroup are unchanged by this invertible sign; the canonical homology shift comparison sends the class of $s_V$ to the class of the same $s_V$. Thus no sign or arbitrary isomorphism has entered this formula.

source.place: Tag 03Q8 (lemma-higher-direct-images), chain-level expansion using the existing resolution-evaluation equality

proof.text: Check restriction directly on this representative. Let $t:V'\to V$ over $S$ and let $\overline a:\mathbf Z[V]\to f_*I^q$ be the ordinary adjunct of $a^0$. If $\eta_f$ is the inverse-image unit, the definition of $g_V$ gives $\overline a_V(e_V)=a^0_{X_V}(\eta_f(e_V))=s_V$ in $(f_*I^q)(V)$. The raw restriction is represented by $a^0\circ f^{-1}\mathbf Z[t]$, whose adjunct is $\overline a\circ\mathbf Z[t]$. In the free represented sheaf, $\mathbf Z[t]_{V'}(e_{V'})=e_V|_{V'}$: both are the generator indexed by $t$. Hence $(\overline a\circ\mathbf Z[t])_{V'}(e_{V'})=\overline a_V(e_V)|_{V'}=s_V|_{V'}$. Direct image restricts along $t_X:X_{V'}\to X_V$, which is etale as a base change of the etale $t$. For the cohomology restriction $P(t)$, clause (5) of the cohomology-pullback functoriality theorem computes $t_X^*$ on the injective resolution $j_V^{-1}I$ with $J=t_X^{-1}j_V^{-1}I$ as restriction of sections through the restriction identifications of the etale inverse-image restriction lemma, and clause (4) with the inverse-image composition isomorphism $c_{j_V,t_X}$ (compatible with the units, hence with these restriction identifications by clause (2) of the restriction lemma) identifies the target with the resolution $j_{V'}^{-1}I$. Under $\Gamma(X_V,j_V^{-1}I)\cong I(X_V)$ of step 1 this induces exactly $[s_V]\mapsto[s_V|_{X_{V'}}]$. With step 3 this is $c_{V'}(A(t)z)=P(t)c_V(z)$. Identity and composition restrictions follow from precomposition and ordinary restriction, so $c$ is a morphism of abelian presheaves.

source.place: Tag 072W (lemma-higher-direct-images), objectwise restriction formula; free generator and adjunction-unit calculation

proof.text: Each component $c_V$ is the constructed map, not just some isomorphism between its source and target. The pointwise-isomorphism theorem for this map applies to the present arbitrary $f,F,V,q$. Together with step 4 it gives an isomorphism of abelian presheaves: the component inverses are natural because $c_{V'}A(t)=P(t)c_V$ implies $A(t)c_V^{-1}=c_{V'}^{-1}P(t)$.

source.place: Tag 03Q8, derived-Hom interpretation; existing explicit comparison-is-iso theorem

proof.text: Compute the specified $\kappa_V$ on $a$. By the derived-adjunction theorem, on a K-injective target $I[q]$ the inverse adjunct is represented by the termwise ordinary counit. Thus the adjunct of $a$ is represented by the ordinary chain adjunct $b:\mathbf Z[V][0]\to f_*(I[q])$, with $b^0=f_*a^0\circ\eta_{f,\mathbf Z[V]}$. Indeed its inverse adjunct is $\varepsilon_{I[q]}\circ f^{-1}b=a$, by counit naturality and the triangle identity; the Hom adjunction is bijective. Direct image and its canonical shift comparison compute this as a map to $(f_*I)[q]$. Taking zeroth homology, undoing the shift, and evaluating $e_V$ gives the cohomology-sheaf class of $b^0_V(e_V)=\overline a_V(e_V)=s_V$. This is exactly the explicitly specified derived-adjunction class map (the class construction in lem-sbc-abelian-higher-direct-image-class-compatibility), and uses no choice of a sheafification isomorphism. The two supporting raw-class lemmas are now proved: additivity follows from additivity of the constructed comparison morphism and its canonicalComparison_class formula. For naturality in the etale object, use the already constructed canonicalComparison and its proved canonicalComparison_class formula from AbelianHigherDirectImageNaturalComparison; this identifies the specified component map with a natural transformation without choosing an existential witness. The main resolution-cocycle compatibility in this step remains to be formalized.

source.place: Tags 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors); termwise adjunction triangle identity and shift on the fixed resolution

proof.text: The site theorem applies to the morphism of sites $X_{\mathrm{et}}\to S_{\mathrm{et}}$ given by the base-change functor $u(V)=X_V$: $u$ is continuous by the etale base-change continuity lemma, its $u_s$ is the inverse image $f^{-1}$ (both sheafify the presheaf inverse image along $u$), which is exact, and $u^s=f_*$ by the definition of the direct image. Its cohomology over the object $u(V)=X_V$ is computed by $I(X_V)$, which step 1 identifies with $\Gamma(X_V,j_V^{-1}I)$, so its presheaf $\mathcal P^q_F$ is $P$. By the canonical cocycle formula of lem-weil-pbc-site-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf, $\iota_V([s_V])$ is precisely the section of $\mathcal H^q(f_*I)$ represented by $s_V$. Steps 3 and 6 now give $\iota_V(c_V(z))=\kappa_V(z)$ for every $z$. Both are independent of the representative: changing $a$ by a chain homotopy changes $s_V$ by a boundary. The same site theorem identifies $P^\#$ with $R^qf_*F$ through the lift of this very $\iota$. Sheafifying the presheaf isomorphism $c$ of step 5 and composing with that lift gives an isomorphism $A^\#\to R^qf_*F$ whose composite with $\eta_A$ is $\kappa$. The universal property of sheafification identifies it with the unique lift $E$. In particular $E$ is invertible and normalized, which does not follow just from existence of a natural comparison.

source.place: Tag 072W (lemma-higher-direct-images), proof: cohomology sheaf is associated to the sectionwise cycles modulo boundaries; Tag 03Q8 etale specialization

proof.text: For a coefficient map $\phi:F\to F'$, choose injective representatives $I,I'$ as in step 1. The K-injective Hom bijection gives a chain map $u:I\to I'$ representing $\phi$ under these resolution comparisons. The raw coefficient image of $a$ is $u[q]\circ a$, whose evaluated cycle is $u^q(s_V)$. The induced restricted cohomology map sends $[s_V]$ to $[u^q(s_V)]$, and the higher-direct-image map is induced by $f_*u$, so sends the sheaf class of $s_V$ to the sheaf class of $u^q(s_V)$. The formulas of steps 3, 6 and 7 therefore commute with coefficients. Homotopic choices give boundaries, hence the same maps, and uniqueness of the sheafification lift also makes $E$ natural in $F$. When $q=0$ these are the ordinary sections and the original adjunction unit calculation. For empty $X_V$, its sections complex is zero, so the same formulas give zero on both sides; the pointwise isomorphism covers this case too.
